title: How Phishing Works: Spot the Fake Email in 60 Seconds 🎣 #shorts
description:
Phishing is the most common way accounts get hacked. A fake email creates urgency, the link points to a look-alike domain, and a cloned login page sends your password straight to the attacker. Learn the three red flags, and why passkeys and two-factor authentication stop it even if you click.

📘 More to learn + my projects: https://github.com/HemashreeVI

#CyberSecurity #Phishing #InfoSec #OnlineSafety #TechExplained #shorts

lines: This email looks exactly like your bank. One click, and your account is gone.
Red flag one: panic. Your account will be locked in twenty four hours. Urgency stops you from thinking.
Red flag two: the link. Hover over it. It's not paypal dot com, it's paypa one dot com, a look-alike domain.
Click it, and you land on a perfect copy of the login page. Whatever you type goes straight to the attacker.
The fix: never log in from an email link. Type the address yourself, and turn on passkeys or 2FA, so a stolen password alone is useless.
Pause. Check the link. Never trust urgency.
